stage_A_state_compression.interpretation: All four reviewed polymorphic systems contain W and C information that a one-tip P code cannot represent as separate extant states. This is state-resolution evidence, not a transition-rate estimate.

stage_B_minimum_transition_count.interpretation: In the only currently testable morph-linked system, population/sample-aware coding doubles the minimum count from 1 to 2. This is single-system direct support for the direction predicted by HMM2, not replicated proof.

stage_C_transition_rate.reason: A replicated rate comparison requires morph-linked population genealogies and branch lengths/topology weights for multiple polymorphic systems.

Cirsium aomorense.reason: The sequenced Moreyra tip is not morph-linked; do not assign it W or C. Targeted public-DB search did not recover a morph-linked white-form sequence, which is not proof of absence.

Cirsium sieboldii.reason: The sequenced tip is from cultivation and is not morph-linked; do not assign it W or C. Targeted public-DB search did not recover a morph-linked white-form sequence, which is not proof of absence.

Cirsium pendulum.reason: The Moreyra sample is from Russia and is not morph-linked; do not assign it W or C. Targeted public-DB search did not recover a morph-linked white-form sequence, which is not proof of absence.

claim_boundary: Do not convert documented within-species W/C polymorphism into a counted evolutionary transition without a genealogy. Do not assign Moreyra tips to white or coloured states when morph linkage is absent. Targeted database non-recovery is not proof that no sequence exists.
